neighbours.label: Fires on ' of' and ' as' in ontological philosophy phrasing (the meaning/question of being, X as such, critique of pure reason), not on ' of' or ' as' in ordinary concrete phrases.
fire: In this lecture, Heidegger returns to the question of being and its forgetting.
For Hegel, the self is never given as such; it must be won through recognition.
The seminar asked whether the being of beings can ever be thought directly.
Kant's transcendental argument concerns the conditions of the possibility of experience.
Phenomenology does not study objects as such but the way they appear to us.
His last book was a meditation on the nature of being and nothingness.
Sartre distinguishes being-in-itself from the mode of being of consciousness.
We never encounter time as such, only change in the things around us.
quiet: In this lecture, the professor returns to the history of the railway and its decline.
For the bakery, the bread is never sold as a loaf; it is cut into slices.
The seminar asked whether the price of tickets could ever be lowered directly.
The builder's report concerns the condition of the roof after the storm.
The museum does not display the coins as a set but one by one in small cases.
His last book was a guide to the rivers and lakes of northern Scotland.
Sartre lived for many years in a small flat on the left bank of the Seine.
We never ate lunch as a family, only a quick snack in the kitchen.
